chimo.titulo_seo: Chimo, Jalisco: how to get there, what is there, when to come
chimo.descripcion_seo: Chimo is a fishing village of 280 people in Cabo Corrientes, 30 km from Puerto Vallarta. How to get there by boat or dirt road, what there is and what there isn't, and when to come.
chimo.hero_texto: A fishing village in Cabo Corrientes, at the southern end of Banderas Bay.

secciones.titulo: Two hundred and eighty people and thirty kilometres of coast
parrafos: Chimo is a locality in the municipality of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco. About 280 people live here year-round, though the number rises during fishing season and if you count the nearby ranches. It sits roughly 30 kilometres south of Puerto Vallarta along the coastline.

You hear the ocean all day. Fishing is the main activity and what gets sold is octopus and fish. The village pier has been half-built for more than twenty years, which limits how much can be landed. There is a health post, though there is rarely a doctor there.
The beaches stay empty most of the year because getting here takes effort. That is exactly the point.

hay_no_hay.titulo: What there is and what there isn't
hay_no_hay.intro: We would rather tell you now than have you find out on arrival.

gente.texto: This section will carry portraits and names of the people of the village: who takes you out in the boat, who cooks, who guides you to the waterfalls. It is the one thing no other house on this coast can copy, which is why it is worth doing properly rather than quickly.

items.texto: The most visited village on the south shore. Same water, far more people.
A waterfall and horseback rides. Written up as the most untouched village in Mexico.
A small beach reachable only by sea.
First stop on the corridor, with beach restaurants.
Heavier surf, and a lighthouse built in 1902.
A bay between cliffs, known for its oysters. A shrimp boat that sank in 1920 is dived here.
An open 12 km beach with a sea turtle camp running since 2005.
The municipal seat at 1,085 m, five to ten degrees cooler. Panela cheese, coffee, honey and raicilla.

items: Cash in pesos. There is no ATM.
Any medication you need. There is no pharmacy.
Closed shoes if you plan to walk to the waterfalls.
A dry bag if you are taking gear out on the boat.

experiencias_pagina.descripcion_seo: Kayaks, whale watching, octopus fishing, waterfalls and the raicilla route. Each one with its season, its duration and who runs it.
experiencias_pagina.hero_texto: Each one with its season, its duration and who runs it. An activity with a date on it is a reason to choose the week.
dia: The fishermen's boat leaves. If you are going, you are up before that.
Breakfast on the terrace with whatever came in.
Kayak to the next cove, before the wind comes up.
Lunch at one of the village kitchens.
Pool, hammock, or the walk to the lookout.
You hear the ocean and nothing else.
